trials.notes: Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), checked null, walked tokens with next_token(), collected #text via get_modifiable_text(), and explicitly whitelisted opening TITLE/TEXTAREA while excluding SCRIPT/STYLE. All HTML API methods used are documented and no _doing_it_wrong records appeared.

Same correct processor and token-walk pattern as the reference. Uses only documented HTML API methods, handles decoded text and special-element opener text correctly, and includes a Unicode-safe regex fallback if mbstring is unavailable. No API misuse recorded.

Uses the right HTML Processor fragment parser and documented token APIs. The HTML API usage is sound: #text plus opening TITLE/TEXTAREA via get_modifiable_text(). Minor non-HTML-API caveat: its no-mbstring fallback uses byte substr(), which would violate the task's Unicode truncation requirement outside this execution environment.

failure_analysis: No hidden case failed in any trial: all three passed 10/10 with no _doing_it_wrong records. The docs succeeded at steering subjects to WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for body fragments, next_token() for token walking, get_token_type()/#text for ordinary text, and get_modifiable_text() for decoded text. The strongest passage was the HTML Processor overview recipe “collect DOM-style text from a subtree,” plus the get_modifiable_text() section explaining that TITLE/TEXTAREA text is decoded and carried on the opener token while SCRIPT/STYLE text is raw and should only be included by explicit policy. Near-misses: the useful guidance is split across the overview recipe, Tag Processor modifiable-text section, and get_modifiable_text() docblock; subjects had to combine “ordinary text excludes special elements” with the task’s explicit opt-in for TITLE/TEXTAREA. They also did not state any explicit unsupported/incomplete-input policy, relying on best-effort accumulation, which the docs allow for read-only extraction but could be made more checklist-like.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::get_modifiable_text() and the “Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree” section
doc_gaps.problem: The contract for text extraction with selected special elements is correct but distributed. Readers must infer how to combine ordinary #text extraction with an explicit whitelist of special-element opener text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general “text extraction policy” note: first choose which token classes belong to the caller’s result; read #text tokens for ordinary DOM text; optionally whitelist opening special elements; TITLE/TEXTAREA return decoded text, while SCRIPT/STYLE return raw text and should not be included unless explicitly requested.

doc_gaps.problem: Completion handling for read-only walks is described, but not as a compact post-walk contract. Models can miss when paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() matter.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an “after a token walk” checklist: returning accumulated text is a valid best-effort policy, but callers requiring complete input should check paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() before trusting the result.

doc_gaps.problem: Both methods work for identifying special element openers in this task, but the preferred distinction during next_token() loops is easy to blur.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Cross-reference the methods with examples: use get_token_type() for node kind, get_tag() for tag-name checks after confirming #tag, and get_token_name() when code intentionally wants DOM-style names such as #text as well as tag names.
